tips.title: Plan with Opus, build with Sonnet
tips.tip: `/model opusplan` runs Opus in plan mode and Sonnet once you approve. `Shift+Tab` toggles plan mode.
tips.when: Multi-file features, refactors, anything you'd sketch first.

tips.title: Dial effort per task
tips.tip: Low effort for boilerplate, `xhigh` for nasty bugs. Pin a default per model so you stop thinking about it.
tips.when: Cost or speed matters, or you're deep in a hard bug.

card.title: claude
lines: > /effort xhigh     # race conditions, perf, gnarly bugs
> /effort auto      # back to the model default

tips.title: Cheap scouts, smart architects
tips.tip: Give every subagent the smallest model that does its job. Haiku explores, Sonnet builds and reviews, Opus plans.
tips.when: Large repos, long sessions, lots of delegation.

code: description: Read-only recon on unfamiliar code. Returns paths + evidence.
Inspect files, commands and tests. Never edit. No generic advice.

tips.title: Less narration, same work
tips.tip: `/output-style concise` puts the result first and drops the play-by-play. Easier to skim after a long run.
tips.when: You skim Claude's replies more than you read them.

card.title: claude
lines: # leads with the result, skips the narration
# full detail is still there when you ask for it

tips.title: Start every session briefed
tips.tip: `SessionStart` output lands in Claude's context. Print branch, dirty files and recent commits so it never starts cold.
tips.when: Always, in any git repo.
tips.note: I also use this hook to flag repos that are missing `AGENTS.md`.

tips.title: Dev server starts itself
tips.tip: An async `SessionStart` hook boots `npm run dev` and logs to a file Claude can read when the UI breaks.
tips.when: `package.json` has a `dev` script (Vite, Next, Astro, …).
tips.done: A `SessionStart` hook runs the dev script.
tips.note: Add to `CLAUDE.md`: *Dev server is already running, errors go to `.claude/dev.log`.* Git-ignore the log.

tips.title: Every edit comes out formatted
tips.tip: `PostToolUse` on `Edit|Write` runs your formatter on the file Claude just touched. Style nits never reach review.
tips.when: Prettier, Biome, Ruff, gofmt: any formatter in the repo.
tips.done: A `PostToolUse` hook matching `Edit`/`Write` runs a formatter.
tips.note: Python: swap in `xargs ruff format`. Needs `jq`.

tips.title: No “done” until types pass
tips.tip: A `Stop` hook runs the type-checker. Exit code 2 hands the errors back and Claude keeps fixing.
tips.when: TypeScript, mypy, `cargo check`: any check that runs in under ~30 s.
tips.done: A `Stop` hook runs a typecheck or test command.
tips.note: Keep it fast. Full test suites belong in CI.

tips.title: Deny the scary stuff
tips.tip: Deny rules beat hoping. Block secrets, force-pushes and `rm -rf`, then run with fewer prompts without sweating.
tips.when: Before you turn on auto mode, `acceptEdits` or skip-permissions.

tips.title: One instruction file for every agent
tips.tip: Rules live in `AGENTS.md`, which Codex, Cursor and co. read too. `CLAUDE.md` just imports it, so the copies never drift.
tips.when: You or your teammates use more than one coding agent.

code: <!-- Claude-only extras below. Keep it short. -->

tips.title: Keep instructions to one screen
tips.tip: Root instructions load every session. Keep commands, hard rules and gotchas there, and point to longer docs by path.
tips.when: `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md` is over ~100 lines, or is untouched `/init` output.
tips.done: An instruction file exists and is under ~150 lines.
tips.note: No file yet? `/init` drafts one. Then cut it in half.

code: npm run dev · npm test · npm run typecheck

tips.title: Guard the context window
tips.tip: `/clear` between tasks, `/context` to see what eats tokens, `/btw` for side questions that shouldn't stick.
tips.when: Long sessions, or answers getting worse.

tips.title: Prompted it twice? Make it a skill
tips.tip: Repeated workflows become `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`. Claude loads it when the description matches, or you run `/<name>`.
tips.when: Releases, changelogs, review checklists, deploys.

code: description: Cut a release. Use when asked to ship or tag a version.
1. Run tests and typecheck. Stop on failure.
2. Bump the version, update CHANGELOG from merged PRs.
3. Tag, push, print the release URL.

tips.title: Parallel sessions, zero collisions
tips.tip: `claude --worktree <name>` gives each session its own checkout and branch. Two features at once, no stepping on toes.
tips.when: One task is running and the next one is ready.

card.title: terminal
lines: # own checkout + branch each · repo needs at least one commit

tips.title: Esc Esc is undo
tips.tip: Double-tap `Esc` or run `/rewind` to roll code and conversation back to a checkpoint. Try the risky idea first.
tips.when: Experiments, big refactors, “let's just try it”.

card.title: claude
lines: # restores Claude's file edits + the conversation

tips.title: Show, don't describe
tips.tip: Paste a screenshot of the broken UI instead of describing it. `Ctrl+V`, or `Alt+V` on Windows.
tips.when: Frontend work, CSS bugs, design handoffs.

card.title: claude
lines: > [Image #1] the card overflows on mobile. fix it.
# Ctrl+V to paste · Alt+V on Windows · or drag the file in

tips.title: ! runs it yourself
tips.tip: Start a line with `!` to run a shell command directly. The output lands in context, and no tokens go into deciding to run it.
tips.when: You already know the exact command.

card.title: claude
lines: # output goes straight into the conversation

tips.title: Review before you commit
tips.tip: `/code-review` hunts real bugs in the diff, and `--fix` applies them. `/security-review` for auth, payments, uploads.
tips.when: Every non-trivial diff.

tips.title: End permission-prompt fatigue
tips.tip: `/fewer-permission-prompts` scans your past sessions and allowlists the read-only commands you always approve.
tips.when: You click “Yes” on the same commands every day.

tips.title: Babysit CI with /loop
tips.tip: `/loop` reruns a prompt on an interval while the session is open. Leave out the interval and Claude paces itself.
tips.when: Waiting on CI, a deploy or a flaky queue.

card.title: claude
lines: > /loop 5m check CI on this branch, fix failures, push
> /loop watch the deploy and tell me when it's green

tips.title: Routines run while you sleep
tips.tip: `/schedule` creates a cloud routine with a cron, GitHub-event or API trigger. It pushes to `claude/` branches and opens PRs.
tips.when: Recurring chores: dependency bumps, docs drift, PR review, triage.
tips.done: Habit, nothing to detect (routines live in your claude.ai account).

card.title: claude
lines: > /schedule every Monday 9am: bump deps, run tests, open a PR
# runs in the cloud · manage at claude.ai/code/routines

tips.title: Let /insights find your next hook
tips.tip: `/insights` builds an HTML report of your recent sessions. Whatever you keep doing by hand is your next hook or skill.
tips.when: Once a month, or whenever your setup feels stale.

card.title: claude
lines: # → HTML report of your recent sessions
# repeated manual steps = hook, skill or routine candidates

tips.title: Pipe it: claude -p
tips.tip: `claude -p` behaves like any Unix tool. Drop it into scripts, git hooks and CI.
tips.when: Anything you'd script: commit messages, log triage, batch edits.
tips.done: `claude -p` appears in scripts, git hooks or CI config.

card.title: terminal
lines: $ git diff --staged | claude -p "write a conventional commit message"
$ cat build.log | claude -p "why did this fail? one line"
